title: Strict-local germ restriction is invertible
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ a geometric point, and $g:S_{(s)}\to S$ the strict-henselization structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. For every abelian étale sheaf $G$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], every map $r:G_s\to\Gamma(S_{(s)},g^{-1}G)$ satisfying the representative-neighbourhood germ restriction equations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-restriction] is an isomorphism. Here $G_s$ is the geometric stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and $g^{-1}$ is inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

proof.text: Choose an affine open containing the image of s. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples] identifies the coordinate-ring colimit of affine pointed neighbourhoods with the colimit of etale residue triples over this affine chart, compatibly with all pointed ring maps. [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] makes the latter a strictly henselian local ring and supplies its residue map to the relative separable closure inside Omega. Transport this local-ring structure and map through the colimit isomorphism. Compose the residue map with its inclusion into Omega to obtain the geometric closed point of the chosen strict-henselization scheme. The compatibility with each pointed ring map makes its composite with the structural map equal to s.

The strict-henselization limit has its geometric closed point above s. Identify the inverse-image stalk there with the original stalk, compatibly with germs, using [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. Strict-local global sections identify with the closed-point stalk by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk]. Compose these two isomorphisms in the direction from the original stalk to global sections.

At every representative affine pointed neighbourhood the germ compatibility of the inverse-image stalk comparison and the pointed limit section show that this composite is the unit followed by restriction along that section. These are the defining section restrictions. Uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-restriction] identifies it with r, which is therefore invertible.
